exposure: methods to access CPD (workshops, online training)
CPD credits acquired related to Emergency Obstetric and Neonatal Care (EmONC) training
outcome: knowledge gaps in key competencies of EmONC
skills gaps in key competencies of EmONC
skills and knowledge gaps in management of Pre/Eclampsia
skills and knowledge gaps in management of Postpartum Hemorrhage
skills and knowledge gaps in essential newborn care
difficulty in achieving required CPD credits
cohort: The study included nurses and midwives from forty health facilities in Rwanda that performed at least 20 deliveries per month from July 1st, 2020 to June 30th, 2021.
finding: The study revealed a low uptake of critical EmONC training through CPD among nurses and midwives in Rwanda, resulting in significant skills and knowledge gaps in crucial areas like Pre/Eclampsia, Postpartum Hemorrhage, and essential newborn care.
cross-section timing: The study assessed the current status of CPD uptake and knowledge at a single point in time, with facilities selected based on their activity between July 2020 and June 2021; the exact data collection period for the cross-section is not specified.
